name: Glendo State Park (Elkhorn Campground)
note: Elkhorn is the northernmost campground on Glendo Reservoir's west shore, off WY 319 about 5 miles north of Glendo and nearest the North Platte inlet. Its grass pads line a gravel spur at the edge of a belt of cottonwoods and willows; the lake reaches the trees in late spring and early summer, but by fall the water can be a half-mile walk away. The one vault toilet is at the boat ramp lot, up to a quarter mile from the farthest sites. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: reserve.wyoming.gov (US eDirect API wyordr.usedirect.com/wyomingrdr/rdr/, PlaceId 10 'Glendo State Park', FacilityId 337 'Elkhorn', facility point 42.55921,-105.03089 = unit EH06, read 2026-11-20): 11 web-bookable units - 8 'Campsite Non-Electric' EH04-EH11 (IsRVSite true, PullInTypeName 'Pull Through', 'Unit & Parking Size(ft)' 100 on all but EH05 (40), 'Parking Pad Material: Grass', 'Campsite Dimensions' 100x20 on EH04-EH10, EH05 and EH11 'ADA Accessible', Rate 10.00, MaximumStay 14) + 3 'Tent Site Non-Electric' TE-1..TE-3 (IsRVSite false) -> real drive-in RV campground a 23-ft rig fits. Wyoming State Parks' own Elkhorn page (wyoparks.wyo.gov/index.php/about-our-campgrounds/1693-elkhorn-glendo, read as search-result text 2026-11-20; the site refuses with an F5 challenge): 9 campsites and one day-use site, reached from I-25 by turning north on Highway 319 out of Glendo for about 5 miles, entrance on the right; amenities 'Vault Toilet (1), Seasonal Boat Ramp and Courtesy Dock, Fee Canister, ADA accessible camping pad (1)'; no 4WD or sand wording (unlike Broken Arrow, Sandy Beach Dune or Red Hills 12-15). The Dyrt review (Oct 29, 2025): 'Good roads.' Imagery: gravel park road off WY 319 to a gravel spur along the tree line, pads on grass beside it. Not in the DB: no name match in WY other than 15734 Casper Mountain Elkhorn Springs (~107 km); nearest entry 13968 Bennett Hill 5.7 km. Public (state): no price gate.
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-20: Esri World Imagery frames at 450 m, 160 m and 100 m half-widths (1.0, 0.36 and 0.22 m/px) with every reserve.wyoming.gov unit point (grid MapInfo, FacilityId 337) plotted; all images rendered. Imagery (leaf-off, reservoir below full pool) shows EH06-EH10 in a row along a gravel spur at the south edge of a continuous belt of leaf-off cottonwoods/willows and reddish brush 30-50 m deep, then a pale sand band and the imaged water ~65-80 m north; EH05 (ADA pad) at the same belt's edge to the west; EH04 on open grass in a clearing ~70 m SW of EH05; EH11 in the boat-ramp gravel lot on higher ground to the east; TE-1..3 tent sites 250 m south. Glendo full pool 4635.0 ft = 1413.51 m NAVD88 (glendo_notes.txt / lead 15). USGS 3DEP lidar (epqs.nationalmap.gov): unit points EH04 1416.0, EH05 1415.6, EH06 1415.7, EH07 1415.3, EH08 1415.2, EH09 1415.5, EH10 1415.6, EH11 1419.5 m (1.7-2.5 m above full pool; EH11 6 m); hydro-flattened water surface 1412.98 m (flown ~0.5 m below full pool) and it reaches into the tree belt. Profiles NNW (340 deg) to the full-pool contour: EH06 ~29 m (1413.98 at 25 m, 1413.36 at 30 m), EH07 ~30 m, EH08 ~27 m, EH09 ~30 m, EH10 ~32 m, EH05 ~29 m; every one of those spans runs into the tree belt, so at high water the trees stand in the lake and the water lies ~30 m off behind trunks and brush -> a continuous treeline buffer, not lakefront (Cottonwood 15738 precedent); leaf-off the stand is open enough, with the pads only ~2 m above the lake, for a filtered view through it -> lakeview. EH04: full pool ~38 m WNW (1413.29 at 40 m) over open grass, the edge there being the margin of a brushy flat with scattered drowned trees that holds water only near full pool; ~50 m to the SW through trees. EH11: full pool ~90 m N downslope (1413.86 at 90 m) -> not waterfront. The engine tags every RV unit 'Waterfront Setting: Reservoir' (type-level, as at Custer Cove). Season: the park ends Elkhorn's reservation season July 15 because 'the lake elevation becoming low and the boat ramp becoming inaccessible' (park page via search text); The Dyrt (Oct 29, 2025): 'about a 1/2mile hike to get to the water from the camp site.'

fees.note: Wyoming's statewide schedule: each night's camping fee is the base rate plus that day's day-use fee plus sales & lodging tax, per vehicle. The booking site shows 'Fees range from $23-41 (Per Night, Per 1 Vehicle)' on every unit.

flags: Reservation season: the park says Elkhorn takes reservations May 15 - July 15 only (FCFS after, as the reservoir drops), but the engine's SeasonDates for FacilityId 337 run the park-wide 2027-05-15..2027-09-15 (false from 09-16). Booking season written as the park's 05-15..07-15; the engine may still sell late-summer nights.

Waterfront close call: lakeview. The row EH05-EH10 is ~27-32 m from the full-pool contour (3DEP lidar), within ~50 m, but every span runs through a continuous cottonwood/willow belt that stands in the water at high pool (treated as a buffer, as at Cottonwood 15738). EH04 alone measures ~38 m to full pool over open grass; that edge is the margin of a brushy flat that holds water only near full pool (May - early July), so it was not counted as a clear waterfront site. If the reviewer reads EH04 as clear, the 'a few clear waterfront sites' rule would allow lakefront with a caveat naming EH04.
Potable water unconfirmed: the park's own amenity list for Elkhorn has none; Campflare and The Dyrt say seasonal water. facilities.potable_water omitted.
